Modern Foreign Languages
At Innsworth Junior School, we use the Language Angels scheme of work to ensure that we offer a broad, vibrant and ambitious foreign languages curriculum that will inspire and excite our pupils using a wide variety of topics and themes.
Our curriculum ensures progress within each academic year, and across the Key Stage, in the four key language learning skills. Listening, speaking, reading and writing, including all necessary grammar, are covered in an age-appropriate way. This will enable pupils to use and apply their learning in a variety of contexts, laying down solid foundations for future language learning.
The intent is that all pupils will develop a genuine interest and positive curiosity about foreign languages, finding them enjoyable and stimulating. Learning a second language will also offer pupils the opportunity to explore relationships between language and identity, develop a deeper understanding of other cultures and the world around them with a better awareness of self, others and cultural differences. The intention is that they will be working towards becoming life-long language learners.

Personal, Social and Health Education
At Innsworth we encourage the children to be independent and resilient learners and to have a good understanding of the world we live in. PSHE enables our children to become healthy, kind and responsible members of society and aims to help them understand how they are developing personally and socially. It also tackles many of the moral, social and cultural issues that are part of growing up.
We incorporate the Jigsaw curriculum, which nurtures children to be confident and successful, into our PSHE offer. This allows children to develop their capacity to learn and prepares them for the challenges of the modern world. Children are provided with opportunities to develop their emotional intelligence, life skills, and gain an understanding of, and opportunities to nurture, their mental wellbeing. We provide our children with opportunities for them to learn about rights and responsibilities and appreciate what it means to be a member of a diverse society. Our children are encouraged to become critical thinkers and develop their sense of self-worth by playing a positive role in contributing to school life and the wider community.

At Innsworth Schools’ Partnership we believe that Design and Technology is crucial in allowing children to develop practical skills for a sustainable future. Our curriculum provides a framework in which children are able to develop their cooking, sewing and engineering skills over time and think critically about design and how good design can improve the world around them.
Our aim is for our children to be confident in talking about, preparing and cooking simple dishes from around the world, reflecting the multi-national character of our school community. We also teach basic sewing techniques so that they will have the skills to be able to mend, recycle and embellish clothes and other fabric articles in the future. In our engineering curriculum, we encourage the children to experiment with a range of mechanisms, materials and components and carry out practical tasks with increasing accuracy through selecting and using a wider range of tools and equipment as they progress through the schools.
Design Technology has the added benefit of allowing children to develop resourcefulness, resilience and problem solving skills. Children are also able to apply skills learned in other disciplines (such as maths, science and art) in a practical way and are encouraged to work constructively with others to analyse and evaluate, make mistakes, share them and learn from them.

English
In addition to Whole Class Reading sessions, we have daily English lessons which are highly focussed on writing. We mainly use Literacy Shed+ for planning using high quality videos and books; other resources may occasionally be used. The texts and videos are well-matched to the age and group of children being taught and provide opportunities which develop rich language models, vocabulary and structures from which children can learn how writing works and the effect it can have on the reader.
We aim to incorporate grammar and punctuation teaching into our writing curriculum as much as possible: children can then see how this looks when it is being used in ‘real’ writing and be able to apply the skills to their own work. There will be occasions when we have stand alone grammar and punctuation lessons.
Spelling is taught using Spelling Shed lessons and linked work; this is supported by the children having access to the Spelling Shed website at home where children can do quizzes and play games related to the words learnt that week at school.
Handwriting is mainly taught in Year 3 and 4 using Nelson Handwriting.
Developing oracy skills is a key driver for us across the curriculum: we aim to develop children’s vocabulary and oracy skills during discussions and presentations. Children are introduced to vocabulary through the writing stimuli which they can use in their own writing.
In class, children have access to their own ‘writer’s toolkit’. In the toolkit children may have model texts; knowledge organisers for different genres of writing; vocabulary/word banks and success criteria for different genres of writing. Children use the skills taught in English across other areas of the curriculum and they have access to their toolkits to support them.
Children’s writing is formally assessed in school three times a year by teachers. Alongside this, children also participate in a ‘No More Marking’ piece of writing: children are given a picture and then write a story based upon it. As staff, we then assess our children’s writing alongside other schools. This gives us the opportunity to make a national comparison. We also participate in an online grammar assessment: using data from this supports children in their understanding of sentence structure.

Maths
Belief + Hard Work + Understanding = Success

At Innsworth Junior School, we foster positive ‘can do’ attitudes, believe all children can achieve in mathematics, and teach for secure and deep understanding of mathematical concepts. We use mistakes and misconceptions as an essential part of learning and provide challenge through rich and sophisticated problems before acceleration through new content.

Using the SACRE Gloucestershire agreed syllabus and Understanding Christianity scheme, our school aims in RE are to allow children to experience and question a range of religious and non-religious worldviews whilst also considering the big questions of life in a safe environment. Our school has high standards in all lessons, including RE, which will aim for children to leave us with a thoughtfully explored spiritual knowledge, an increased general knowledge as well as a bank of skills to understand and tolerate the beliefs of others in order to live in today’s diverse and ever changing world. This is completed through different creative mediums including (and not limited to) art, drama, exploring challenging texts, discussion and formal writing opportunities.

Reading
At Innsworth Junior School, we recognise the importance of learning to read and its impact on a child’s future learning. We expect all children to develop and secure the variety of skills needed to be a fluent reader and our aim is that all children will find books that they enjoy reading for pleasure.
All our children take part in reading activities daily, this may be in class taking part in Whole Class Reading sessions or in small groups taking part in phonics sessions. In addition to this, children have opportunities within school to read alongside adults on a 1:1 basis. Each class also has allocated time everyday to sit down and enjoy a story. Staff read this story so that children hear good quality, expressive, fluent reading daily.
Whole class reading is where the core reading teaching happens for the majority of children. There are 2 distinct parts to whole class reading at our school. Children will have 2 sessions a week that are based on their class novel. They will discuss the author’s intent and make predictions based on what has already been read. The children will then have 3 sessions based on one text. They will spend one session becoming familiar with the text by reading it several times and answering some retrieval questions. They will then have a session where they discuss inferences, make summaries and give explanations. The final session will be an independent session where they answer a variety of question types to demonstrate their understanding of the text.
We use RWI as our phonics scheme for the children who need to develop their phonic knowledge. This allows all staff who teach it to follow a structure, giving the children the best possible chance of success. We organise this in small and focused groups allowing us to meet the needs of individual children. We monitor and assess the children regularly to move them along the scheme as needed. This is also supported with reading books linked to the sounds the children have learnt so they can practise and reinforce their knowledge and skills for blending to read.
We know that Reading requires a range of skills which weave together to make a successful reader. We offer children a range of reading books to take home which will support the acquisition of skills appropriate to their stage of reading. This process is regularly assessed to ensure progress and appropriate provision for each child. Children are encouraged to read regularly at home to practise the skills they have been taught in school and to develop a love for reading and to read for pleasure.

At Innsworth Schools’ Partnership, we believe that music, in its many forms, is a vital part of our cultures and therefore studying music allows us an additional window into learning about the world, it peoples, and its history, as well as being a tool for self-expression and an important subject in its own right.
Singing, in particular group singing, can be instrumental in fostering a sense of belonging and has been shown to improve mental health and this is why we have chosen an approach which puts singing at the heart of our provision.
The children learn about music by listening to, singing and playing music from different cultures and time periods. Through this, they develop their knowledge of the inter-related dimensions of music (pitch, duration, dynamics, tempo, timbre, texture, structure and appropriate musical notations). As they move through the schools, children become more adept at discussing music and using their ideas and musical knowledge to compose short pieces and songs.
In addition to the main music curriculum, there are other opportunities for children to engage in music making across the partnership, for example: school productions, concerts, clubs and individual music lessons.

Breakfast and After School Clubs
(Wrap Around Child Care)
At Innsworth Junior School we offer wrap around child care, which is open from 7.30am until 6.00pm, Monday to Friday in term-time for children at our infant and junior schools. Our clubs are run by qualified staff.
Please ensure that bookings are made by Friday lunchtime on the week before your child needs the sessions by logging in to your School Money account.
Bookings
Information on how to access our online secure booking system will be generated and sent to you once your child has officially started school.
Payments
We are a cashless school and we use an online platform called School Money to collect secure online payments for breakfast and afterschool club. We ask that payments are made via this system rather than sending cash or cheques into school. You will receive a text from School Money with details of how to make your payment. Please refer to our club terms and conditions.
We accept childcare vouchers...
If your employer operates a childcare voucher scheme you will be able to use the vouchers to pay for your child’s attendance at our Breakfast and After School Club. ‘Childcare vouchers’ is a Government scheme, operated through employers, enabling working parents to pay for childcare from their pre-tax salaries. We are registered to accept childcare vouchers from the following providers:
Voucher Provider
KiddiVoucher Computershare
Sodexo Childcare Choices (Government TFC)
Breakfast Club
Our Breakfast Club operates from the Junior School from 7.30 am – 8.40 am. We provide a safe and enjoyable start to the day, which includes a choice of breakfast such as toast, cereals, yogurts and fruit juices. The Club also includes activities and games for the children.
After School Club
Our After School Club is open from 3.10pm – 6.00pm with flexible sessions for parents to collect at their convenience. They are offered a light snack. On occasions, we have treat night when the children enjoy flapjacks and hot chocolate. Children have a choice of toys, games, books, arts and crafts which they can access independently. We also provide structured activities such as cooking, outdoor play and gardening. Staff plan treat activities to enhance provision on special occasions.

Governors
Governing Body – Innsworth Schools’ Partnership
The majority of children from Innsworth Infant School transfer to Innsworth Junior School to complete their primary phase education. Each school had its own Governing Body. While the two schools had always worked together, in 2013 it was agreed that even closer cooperation could be achieved, resulting in a better educational ‘offering’ to pupils, by federating the two governing bodies into one. This occurred on September 1, 2014 and the Innsworth Schools’ Partnership came into being. The ties between the schools were further strengthened by the appointment of Mrs Lisa Jones as Executive Headteacher on September 1, 2015, with responsibility for both schools.
The overall role of Governors is to support the Headteacher and the staff – the phrase often used to describe this role is ‘a critical friend’. Governors help the Headteacher and Staff to set and reach targets and to strive for excellence across the whole spectrum of school life. The two key documents used for this are the Partnership Development Plan (PDP) and the Self Evaluation Form (SEF). The PDP sets out a strategic plan for the school, with targets that everyone works towards and the SEF sets out how well the school is doing and where we aim to make improvements.
Statutory duties of the Governing Body include:-
The Governing Body meets at least once every term (6 meetings per academic year). Committees look at particular areas of school life under the headings, Learning, Resourcing and Staffing. All governors are informed about what happens at these meetings.
Learning Committee - looks at pupil progress and attainment, and the quality and consistency of teaching.Resourcing and Staffing Committee – looks at how the school budgets are being spent, within the classroom, and on buildings and facilities. Looks at all aspects of school life affecting and affected by staff.There are several categories of governor, representing different groups that have an interest in the schools. These are the Headteacher, Parent Governors (elected by parents) and a Staff Governor (elected by staff from both schools). This group of Governors convened the first meeting of the FGB and then co-opted further governors to complete the FGB. One of those co-opted governors is nominated by the local authority, Gloucestershire County Council. Co-opted governors are appointed because of their specific expertise or the experience which they can bring to the FGB.
The children at both schools are at the heart of everything the Headteacher, Staff and Governors do. We are committed to providing an environment, where all aspects, physical, emotional, academic and playful, can be enjoyed by all of our children so that by the end of the primary stage of their education, they have all had the opportunity to ‘enjoy, achieve, aspire’. This is the inspiration behind the establishment of the Innsworth Schools’ Partnership.

At Innsworth Schools’ Partnership, we believe that art provides all children with an alternative means of expressing and sharing their ideas, thoughts and feelings. We encourage children to see themselves as artists and to become comfortable with their creativity, in whatever form it may take.
The children take inspiration from a range of artists, both living and historical, from a range of cultures which reflect the diversity of our school community. We aim to develop understanding of fundamental visual concepts in art and design (line, colour, texture, pattern, shape and 3D form) by talking about, and evaluating critically, the work of different artists. We then move to a more practical approach which focuses on drawing skills and experimenting with, and developing control of, a range of media.
Children use sketchbooks from Reception all the way up to Year 6. We encourage the children to think of their sketchbooks as a place where they can record their thoughts, feelings and ideas (both written and visual) as well as where they can experiment with different ideas or media and practice different techniques.

At Innsworth Junior School, we believe that computing is an important life skill that will help to set our children up for secondary school but also jobs of the future and enable them to access technology that is developing quickly in order to function in society. Many of our children love accessing technology and this is a way to engage them in their learning across all aspects of the curriculum.
E-safety is taught six times a year. This is vitally important to enable the children to stay safe online. A range of topics are covered but important themes such as staying safe online and cyberbullying are visited regularly throughout their time in school. We use an online environment, Seesaw, to share learning with each other and families at home. This is also a safe space to teach about social media; what is safe and appropriate to share and comment online.
Children access a range of technology through their time in school including iPads, laptops and micro:bits both in computing classes and in a cross-curricular way. This reflects the real-life applications of the technology they come into contact with and helps to make learning accessible.
Children are taught to solve problems they encounter in their work and to help each other to create strategies and solutions. Children are taught to see computers and iPads as a safe place to make mistakes and work to correct them.
